claims.claim: The relative change in expression upon mutation of the Gli motifs, both in vitro and in vivo, was usually greater in modules with higher-quality Gli sites such as DB and ZY, compared to modules with weaker sites such as HF and YU.
claims.source: However, the relative change in expression upon mutation of the Gli motifs, both in vitro and in vivo, was usually greater in modules with higher-quality Gli sites such as DB and ZY, compared to modules with weaker sites such as HF and YU (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: While Gli motif quality plays a role in Hh/Gli responsiveness, it is not in itself a good indicator of which enhancers will be the most strongly active in a given tissue.
claims.source: Taking these results altogether, we conclude that, while Gli motif quality plays a role in Hh/Gli responsiveness (positively or negatively, depending on the developmental context), it is not in itself a good indicator of which enhancers will be the most strongly active in a given tissue.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claims.claim: The high-affinity Gli sites in the DB module may require additional flanking sequence in order to exert a strong influence on gene expression in vivo.
claims.source: This result led us to hypothesize that the high-affinity Gli sites in the DB module may require additional flanking sequence in order to exert a strong influence on gene expression in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the experimental observations.

claims.claim: All of the fragments (DB, GB, HB, and JB) drove ptc-like stripes in the wing, but the levels and dorsal-ventral extents of gene expression increased greatly with the addition of 5' flanking sequence.
claims.source: All of the fragments (DB, GB, HB, and JB, in order of increasing size) drove ptc-like stripes in the wing, but while the anterior-posterior positions of these stripes were the same, the levels and dorsal-ventral extents of gene expression increased greatly with the addition of 5' flanking sequence (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: 5' sequences containing relatively few and weak Gli motifs provided significant boosts to gene expression in the wing.
claims.source: 5' sequences containing relatively few and weak Gli motifs provided significant boosts to gene expression in the wing: for example, compare GB to DB, and HB to GB (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: Mutating the three optimal Gli sites in modules DB, GB, and JB significantly reduced peak gene expression in the wing stripe.
claims.source: We next examined the direct contribution of the three optimal Gli sites (located within region D) to the in vivo activity of the nested fragments DB, GB, and JB. In all cases, mutating these three Gli sites (while leaving any other Gli motifs intact) significantly reduced peak gene expression in the wing stripe (Figure 4K) (Student's t-test; p<0.0015).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4K and statistical analysis.

claims.claim: The relative contribution of the three optimal Gli sites decreased as more cis-regulatory context was included—from a 99.9% reduction in module DB, to a 62% reduction in module GB, to a 26% reduction in module JB.
claims.source: However, the relative contribution of those three sites, measured as reduction of expression of a 3xGli-mutant enhancer compared to wild-type, decreased as more cis-regulatory context was included—from a 99.9% reduction in module DB, to a 62% reduction in module GB, to a 26% reduction in module JB (Figure 4K).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4K.

claims.claim: Three optimal Ci/Gli sites are not capable of activating gene expression in the wing when taken out of their native sequence context.
claims.source: When taken out of their native sequence context and tested as a synthetic reporter, three optimal Ci/Gli sites are not capable of activating gene expression in the wing, though they can strongly synergize with other activator binding sites (Ramos and Barolo, 2013).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claims.claim: All sub-fragments of module JB (JI, H, GE, and DB) were sufficient to drive expression in the wing disc.
claims.source: By breaking down module JB into smaller, non-overlapping sub-fragments (JI, H, GE, and DB; see Figure 4F), we were able to test the individual contributions of these regions, with very different predicted Gli binding patterns, to gene activation. Note that of these fragments, only module DB contains the cluster of three optimal Gli motifs. All of these modules were sufficient to drive expression in the wing disc, and as with the more distal patched wing enhancers examined above, little or no correlation between predicted Gli affinity and in vivo expression levels was observed (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4F and 4G.

claims.claim: Transcriptional synergy among sub-fragments was observed in vivo, such that the activity of a large fragment (JB, HB, GB) was greater than the sum of the individual activities of its constituent sub-fragments.
claims.source: In general, transcriptional synergy among sub-fragments was observed in vivo, such that the activity of a large fragment (JB, HB, GB) was greater than the sum of the individual activities of its constituent sub-fragments (Figure 4H–J).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4H-J.

claims.claim: Even in the wing, the promoter-proximal cluster of optimal Gli sites makes a relatively minor (though significant) contribution to the Hh/Gli response of patched.
claims.source: The above findings suggest that, even in the wing, the promoter-proximal cluster of optimal Gli sites makes a relatively minor (though significant) contribution to the Hh/Gli response of patched, and that inputs from many additional cis-regulatory regions, some of which contain relatively few and/or weak Gli motifs, are integrated to produce the final pattern of transcriptional activation in this tissue.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claims.claim: Inputs from many additional cis-regulatory regions, some of which contain relatively few and/or weak Gli motifs, are integrated to produce the final pattern of transcriptional activation in the wing.
claims.source: The above findings suggest that, even in the wing, the promoter-proximal cluster of optimal Gli sites makes a relatively minor (though significant) contribution to the Hh/Gli response of patched, and that inputs from many additional cis-regulatory regions, some of which contain relatively few and/or weak Gli motifs, are integrated to produce the final pattern of transcriptional activation in this tissue.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claims.claim: Some ptc enhancers drove qualitatively and quantitatively different in vivo expression patterns when placed in cis to a homologous vs. a heterologous promoter.
claims.source: In addition to the multi-modular complexity of the ptc locus, we found evidence of higher-level control of gene expression via specialized enhancer-promoter interactions. Some ptc enhancers drove qualitative and quantitatively different in vivo expression patterns when placed in cis to a homologous vs. a heterologous promoter (e.g., Figures 2M,3K; see also below).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figures 2M and 3K.

claims.claim: In third-instar larvae, the ptc promoter and 5' sequences are bound by the Polycomb group (PcG) factors Pleiohomeotic (Pho), Polyhomeotic (Ph), Polycomb (Pc), and Posterior sex combs (Psc), as well as the Trithorax group (TrxG) factor Trl/GAF.
claims.source: In third-instar larvae, the ptc promoter and 5' sequences are bound by the Polycomb group (PcG) factors Pleiohomeotic (Pho), Polyhomeotic (Ph), Polycomb (Pc), and Posterior sex combs (Psc), as well as the Trithorax group (TrxG) factor Trl/GAF (Oh et al., 2013; Schaaf et al., 2013), and are marked with the repressive histone modification H3K27me3 (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research and illustrated in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: In third-instar larvae, the ptc promoter and 5' sequences are marked with the repressive histone modification H3K27me3.
claims.source: In third-instar larvae, the ptc promoter and 5' sequences are bound by the Polycomb group (PcG) factors Pleiohomeotic (Pho), Polyhomeotic (Ph), Polycomb (Pc), and Posterior sex combs (Psc), as well as the Trithorax group (TrxG) factor Trl/GAF (Oh et al., 2013; Schaaf et al., 2013), and are marked with the repressive histone modification H3K27me3 (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from ChIP-seq data illustrated in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: In embryos, the ptc promoter lacks PRE signatures: compared to the PRE-containing loci en/inv, AbdB, and Ubx, the ptc promoter region has low PcG occupancy (except for Pho) and low H3K27me3.
claims.source: In embryos, however, the ptc promoter lacks PRE signatures: compared to the PRE-containing loci en/inv, AbdB, and Ubx, the ptc promoter region has low PcG occupancy (except for Pho) and low H3K27me3 (Schuettengruber et al., 2009) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research and illustrated in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: A motif analysis of DNA sequences located 5' of the ptc promoter identified conserved binding motifs for the PcG protein Pho and the TrxG transcription factor Trl/GAF.
claims.source: A motif analysis of DNA sequences located 5' of the ptc promoter using the CIS-BP database (Weirauch et al., 2014) identified conserved binding motifs for the PcG protein Pho (ortholog of vertebrate YY1) and the TrxG transcription factor Trl/GAF (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 2), consistent with our tissue-specific ChIP-seq binding data.
claims.evidence: This is an analysis of sequence data illustrated in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The ptc core promoter region lacks a TATA box but contains a Drosophila Initiator element (Inr) and multiple GAF-binding GAGA motifs, as well as a pause button (PB) and a Downstream Promoter Element (DPE) 3' of the transcription start site.
claims.source: The ptc core promoter region lacks a TATA box but contains a Drosophila Initiator element (Inr) and multiple GAF-binding GAGA motifs, as well as a pause button (PB) and a Downstream Promoter Element (DPE) 3' of the transcription start site (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is an analysis of sequence data illustrated in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The GAGA + Inr + [PB and/or DPE] promoter configuration is associated with RNA polymerase II stalling at Drosophila promoters.
claims.source: The GAGA + Inr + [PB and/or DPE] promoter configuration is associated with RNA polymerase II stalling at Drosophila promoters (Hendrix et al., 2008), and embryonic GRO-seq data identify ptc as one of the most heavily promoter-paused genes in the Drosophila genome (Saunders et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Embryonic GRO-seq data identify ptc as one of the most heavily promoter-paused genes in the Drosophila genome.
claims.source: The GAGA + Inr + [PB and/or DPE] promoter configuration is associated with RNA polymerase II stalling at Drosophila promoters (Hendrix et al., 2008), and embryonic GRO-seq data identify ptc as one of the most heavily promoter-paused genes in the Drosophila genome (Saunders et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: When paired with the heterologous hspmin promoter, the ptc embryonic stripe enhancers PN and LJ activate expression in restricted subsets of the ptc segment-polarity stripe pattern.
claims.source: When paired with the heterologous hspmin promoter, the ptc embryonic stripe enhancers PN and LJ activate expression in restricted subsets of the ptc segment-polarity stripe pattern (dorsal and posterior ptc-positive cells, respectively, within each embryonic segment) (Figure 5C, left).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Neither the core ptc promoter, fragment A, nor the upstream element, fragment B, were sufficient to enhance the Hh/Gli response of module PN.
claims.source: Neither the core ptc promoter, fragment A, nor the upstream element, fragment B, were sufficient to enhance the Hh/Gli response of module PN (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A–H), suggesting that both the ptc core promoter, region A, and the promoter-proximal fragment B are required for this enhancement.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-H.

claims.claim: Both the ptc core promoter, region A, and the promoter-proximal fragment B are required for enhancement of the Hh/Gli response of module PN.
claims.source: Neither the core ptc promoter, fragment A, nor the upstream element, fragment B, were sufficient to enhance the Hh/Gli response of module PN (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A–H), suggesting that both the ptc core promoter, region A, and the promoter-proximal fragment B are required for this enhancement.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-H.

claims.claim: Three of four tested wing-stripe enhancers (GC, YU, and ZY) showed reduced activity when paired with the ptcBA promoter, compared to the heterologous hspmin promoter.
claims.source: We next examined the promoter effects on ptc enhancer function in larval imaginal discs—where, in contrast to the embryo, we found strong PcG binding and the Polycomb-produced repressive mark H3K27me3 at and upstream of the promoter (Figure 5A; compare with Figure 5—figure supplement 1). Three of four tested wing-stripe enhancers (GC, YU, and ZY) showed reduced activity when paired with the ptcBA promoter, compared to the heterologous hspmin promoter (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: A fourth wing enhancer, HF, showed no difference in peak levels of activation, but had a higher baseline expression level across the wing when paired with ptcBA.
claims.source: A fourth wing enhancer, HF, showed no difference in peak levels of activation, but had a higher baseline expression level across the wing when paired with ptcBA (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Interactions among multiple regions of the cis-regulatory apparatus, including distal enhancers, 5' promoter-proximal sequences, and the core promoter are integrated to determine the final pattern and levels of gene expression in each tissue, in a manner that correlates with the presence or absence of PcG/TrxG regulation of a tissue- or stage-specific PRE.
claims.source: Taken together, our genomics and functional results suggest that interactions among multiple regions of the cis-regulatory apparatus, including distal enhancers, 5' promoter-proximal sequences, and the core promoter are integrated to determine the final pattern and levels of gene expression in each tissue, in a manner that correlates with the presence or absence of PcG/TrxG regulation of a tissue- or stage-specific PRE.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genomics and functional data.

claims.claim: The TrxG factor GAF directly occupies the intronic embryonic stripe enhancer 1EH in the embryo.
claims.source: Interestingly, the TrxG factor GAF—which has been associated with transcriptional activation in addition to its role in PRE-mediated repression (Adkins et al., 2006)—directly occupies the intronic embryonic stripe enhancer 1EH in the embryo, though to a lesser extent than the ptc promoter (Figure 5A; Figure 5—figure supplement 1), probably via conserved GAGA motifs in that element (Figure 5—source data 1 and Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from ChIP-seq data illustrated in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1, supported by sequence analysis.

claims.claim: The 1EH module does not require the heavily GAF-occupied ptc promoter for strong activation in the embryo.
claims.source: This may explain why the 1EH module, the most powerful embryonic stripe enhancer at the ptc locus, does not require the heavily GAF-occupied ptc promoter for strong activation in the embryo (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the GAF occupancy data and experimental results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: GAF has recently been implicated in large-scale changes in gene regulation during the embryo-larva transition.
claims.source: GAF has recently been implicated in large-scale changes in gene regulation during the embryo-larva transition (Blanch et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Direct transcriptional activation of ptc by Hh/Gli, for the purpose of negative feedback regulation, is a regulatory circuit that predates the protostome-deuterostome split.
claims.source: Direct transcriptional activation of ptc by Hh/Gli, for the purpose of negative feedback regulation, is a regulatory circuit that predates the protostome-deuterostome split (Alexandre et al., 1996; Goodrich et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Two Gli-bound enhancers of mouse Ptch1 have been reported: a high-affinity promoter-proximal neural tube module and a lower-affinity intronic limb bud mesenchyme module.
claims.source: Two Gli-bound enhancers of mouse Ptch1 have been reported: a high-affinity promoter-proximal neural tube module (Vokes et al., 2007) and a lower-affinity intronic limb bud mesenchyme module (Lopez-Rios et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: ChIP-seq analysis and previous studies identify many sites of significant Gli binding near mPtch1 and extending far upstream of the gene.
claims.source: Our ChIP-seq analysis and previous studies (Lopez-Rios et al., 2014; Peterson et al., 2012; Vokes et al., 2007) identify many sites of significant Gli binding near mPtch1 and extending far upstream of the gene (Figure 6A,B).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by the authors' ChIP-seq data and citations to prior research, illustrated in Figure 6A,B.

claims.claim: All tested Ptch1 modules are active in different, overlapping subsets of the Ptch1 expression pattern: no single module recapitulates the complete Hh/Gli-responsive expression pattern of the parent gene.
claims.source: We tested seven of these Gli-bound regions as lacZ reporters in transgenic mice. As with enhancers of Drosophila ptc, we found that all tested Ptch1 modules are active in different, overlapping subsets of the Ptch1 expression pattern: no single module, no matter how strongly bound by Gli, recapitulates the complete Hh/Gli-responsive expression pattern of the parent gene (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Binding of Gli transcription factors to numerous sites in the Ptch1 locus is dynamic across several different developmental contexts.
claims.source: Binding of Gli transcription factors to numerous sites in the Ptch1 locus is dynamic across several different developmental contexts, perhaps suggesting that enhancer modules are differentially accessible in a developmentally regulated manner (Figure 6B, red arrows).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from ChIP-seq data illustrated in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The novel enhancers identified in this study and the previously identified modules do not account for the complete Ptch1 pattern, suggesting that there are still more yet uncharacterized Ptch1 enhancers to be found.
claims.source: Even taken together, the novel enhancers that we identify here and the previously identified modules do not account for the complete Ptch1 pattern, suggesting that there are still more yet uncharacterized Ptch1 enhancers to be found—presumably with relatively lower levels of Gli factor binding, since the highest-occupancy ChIP-seq peaks have now been tested.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claims.claim: Chromatin at the mouse Ptch1 locus is H3K27-trimethylated at the promoter and in upstream noncoding regions, characteristic of PcG regulation.
claims.source: As in fly ptc, chromatin at the mouse Ptch1 locus is H3K27-trimethylated at the promoter and in upstream noncoding regions (Figure 6C, compare with Figure 5A), characteristic of PcG regulation (Bowman et al., 2014; Brown and Kassis, 2013).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from ChIP-seq data illustrated in Figure 6C, supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Mouse Ptch1 and fly patched share a general gene-expression profile (broad, weak basal expression plus a constitutive response to Hh/Gli).
claims.source: Mouse Ptch1 and fly patched share a general gene-expression profile (broad, weak basal expression plus a constitutive response to Hh/Gli), as well as a complex multi-enhancer organization in which the universal response to Hedgehog signaling is not constituted in a master Gli response element, but distributed across many sub-tissue-specific Gli-regulated modules (Figure 6A,D,E).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the comparative findings illustrated in Figure 6A,D,E.

claims.claim: Mouse Ptch1 and fly patched share a complex multi-enhancer organization in which the universal response to Hedgehog signaling is distributed across many sub-tissue-specific Gli-regulated modules.
claims.source: Mouse Ptch1 and fly patched share a general gene-expression profile (broad, weak basal expression plus a constitutive response to Hh/Gli), as well as a complex multi-enhancer organization in which the universal response to Hedgehog signaling is not constituted in a master Gli response element, but distributed across many sub-tissue-specific Gli-regulated modules (Figure 6A,D,E).
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by comparative experimental data illustrated in Figure 6A,D,E.

claims.claim: Both Ptch1 and patched are flanked by a nearby 3' boundary (associated with a closely neighboring downstream gene) and a far more remote 5' boundary.
claims.source: Hi-C topographical domain mapping and ChIP-seq occupancy data for the chromatin insulator/boundary factor CTCF indicate that both Ptch1 and patched are flanked by a nearby 3' boundary (associated with a closely neighboring downstream gene) and a far more remote 5' boundary (Dixon et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2012) (Figure 6A,D,E; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research and illustrated in Figure 6A,D,E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: In both fly and mouse, all mapped enhancers fall within the topographical domain defined by CTCF boundaries.
claims.source: In both fly and mouse, all mapped enhancers fall within this topographical domain; they rely on Gli sites across a wide range of affinities; they appear to also require additional tissue-specific transcription factor inputs (Supplementary file 2); and they act through a PcG-bound, H3K27me3-marked promoter.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the comparative findings from the study.

claims.claim: The enhancers of patched/Ptch1 rely on Gli sites across a wide range of affinities.
claims.source: In both fly and mouse, all mapped enhancers fall within this topographical domain; they rely on Gli sites across a wide range of affinities; they appear to also require additional tissue-specific transcription factor inputs (Supplementary file 2); and they act through a PcG-bound, H3K27me3-marked promoter.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from the study.

claims.claim: The enhancers of patched/Ptch1 appear to require additional tissue-specific transcription factor inputs.
claims.source: In both fly and mouse, all mapped enhancers fall within this topographical domain; they rely on Gli sites across a wide range of affinities; they appear to also require additional tissue-specific transcription factor inputs (Supplementary file 2); and they act through a PcG-bound, H3K27me3-marked promoter.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the analysis of enhancer sequences.

claims.claim: The enhancers of patched/Ptch1 act through a PcG-bound, H3K27me3-marked promoter.
claims.source: In both fly and mouse, all mapped enhancers fall within this topographical domain; they rely on Gli sites across a wide range of affinities; they appear to also require additional tissue-specific transcription factor inputs (Supplementary file 2); and they act through a PcG-bound, H3K27me3-marked promoter.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from the study.

claims.claim: This study demonstrates for the first time how a constitutive pathway-responsive gene is precisely regulated in diverse developmental contexts.
claims.source: This study, which examines the regulation of an essential developmental gene at the locus-wide level, demonstrates for the first time how a constitutive pathway-responsive gene is precisely regulated in diverse developmental contexts.
claims.evidence: This is a claim about the novelty and significance of the study's findings.

claims.claim: ptc must be broadly active to inhibit Smoothened activity, preventing the inappropriate activation of Hh target genes and subsequent faulty patterning, developmental defects, and disease.
claims.source: This regulation consists of two major modes of control: First, ptc must be broadly active to inhibit Smoothened activity, preventing the inappropriate activation of Hh target genes and subsequent faulty patterning, developmental defects, and disease (Katoh and Katoh, 2009; Barakat et al., 2010; Scales and de Sauvage, 2009; Teglund and Toftgård, 2010).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: The promoter-proximal 5' sequence, region B, in conjunction with the core promoter acts as the likely controller of the basal, signal-independent mode of ptc expression.
claims.source: Our reporter-based analysis of the locus has identified a promoter-proximal 5' sequence, region B, which in conjunction with the core promoter acts as the likely controller of the basal, signal-independent mode of ptc expression.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reporter-based analysis.

claims.claim: The constitutive Hh response of ptc is accomplished by a collection of Gli-regulated enhancers spread across the ptc gene locus.
claims.source: Second, ptc must be able to respond to Hh/Gli signaling in many developmental and stem-niche contexts. We show here that this is not accomplished by a master Hh/Gli response element, but rather by a collection of Gli-regulated enhancers spread across the ptc gene locus.
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by extensive experimental data.

claims.claim: Remote, tissue- and sub-tissue-specific enhancers of ptc work synergistically and are integrated with additional information from promoter-proximal sequences and the core promoter, responding to Hh signaling differently in each stage and tissue type.
claims.source: These remote, tissue- and sub-tissue-specific enhancers work synergistically and are integrated with additional information from promoter-proximal sequences and the core promoter, responding to Hh signaling differently in each stage and tissue type.
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: The quality/affinity of Gli binding motifs in ptc enhancers is extremely important for proper patterning, to the extent that optimizing Gli motifs in certain enhancers can cripple enhancer activity.
claims.source: At least in some enhancer modules, we find that the quality/affinity of Gli binding motifs in these enhancers is extremely important for proper patterning, to the extent that optimizing Gli motifs in certain enhancers can cripple enhancer activity.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on Gli site optimization.

claims.claim: Low-to-moderate-affinity transcription factor binding sites can be important for limiting the response of a target gene to a pleiotropic, broadly active transcription factor or pathway.
claims.source: Previous studies from our group and others have shown that low-to-moderate-affinity transcription factor binding sites can be important for limiting the response of a target gene to a pleiotropic, broadly active transcription factor or pathway (Swanson et al., 2011; Crocker et al., 2015; Farley et al., 2015; additional references within).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: The results with embryonic stripe enhancers of the ptc gene point to a different type of regulatory control by weak binding sites, in which the occupancy of a transcription factor is modulated to an optimal level of activation within a tissue.
claims.source: Our results with embryonic stripe enhancers of the ptc gene, however, point to a different type of regulatory control by weak binding sites, in which the occupancy of a transcription factor is modulated to an optimal level of activation within a tissue.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claims.claim: The fact that optimal activation is achieved via suboptimal Gli binding sites in the Drosophila embryo may reflect the fact that Ci/Gli acts both as an activator and as a repressor through the same binding sites.
claims.source: The fact that optimal activation is achieved via suboptimal Gli binding sites in the Drosophila embryo may reflect the fact that Ci/Gli acts both as an activator and as a repressor through the same binding sites.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed explanation for the experimental observations.

claims.claim: The GliA:GliR ratio may be significantly lower in Hh-responsive cells in the embryonic segments than in late-larval wing discs.
claims.source: Considering that the area and duration of Hh production in embryonic segments is vastly lower than that in larval/pupal wings, where half of the organ produces Hh protein for most of the developmental period of the animal, it is to be expected that the GliA:GliR ratio may be significantly lower in Hh-responsive cells in the embryonic segments than in late-larval wing discs.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the differences in Hh production between tissues.

claims.claim: The relatively high concentration of GliR in Hh-responding embryonic cells may create selective pressures favoring lower Gli occupancy.
claims.source: If so, the relatively high concentration of GliR in Hh-responding embryonic cells may create selective pressures favoring lower Gli occupancy, as we have argued previously (Parker et al., 2011; White et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is a speculation supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claims.claim: The same large-scale cis-regulatory strategy at work in the fly ptc locus is also present in vertebrate Ptch1.
claims.source: Our results from transgenic mouse reporter constructs and Gli ChIP-seq experiments suggest that the same large-scale cis-regulatory strategy at work in the fly locus is also present in vertebrates—at least to the extent that many enhancers, with widely varying levels of Gli input, act in combination but in a tissue-specific manner to independently adjust Ptch1 expression levels in each cell type, giving the illusion of a universal response to Hh signaling but in fact representing a complex array of context-limited responses.
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on comparative experimental data from mouse and fly.

claims.claim: The specific cis-regulatory sequences that regulate patched and its orthologs are not conserved across large evolutionary distances from insects to mammals.
claims.source: However, we do not mean to propose that the specific cis-regulatory sequences that regulate patched and its orthologs are conserved across such large evolutionary distances. Individual patched enhancers show no obvious sequence conservation from insects to mammals—unsurprisingly, given that most ptc-expressing, Hh/Gli-regulated organs present in modern animals did not exist at the time of the protostome-deuterostome divergence.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from sequence analysis and evolutionary considerations.

claims.claim: patched and its orthologs share an ancient regulatory structure composed of relatively young enhancers.
claims.source: Rather, we propose that patched and its orthologs share an ancient regulatory structure composed of relatively young enhancers.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the comparative findings.

claims.claim: patched enhancer evolution likely involved both tuning of Gli occupancy and the co-option of tissue-specific inputs to produce new aspects of the patched expression pattern over time.
claims.source: Based on our motif analyses and mutational studies, we propose that patched enhancer evolution likely involved both tuning of Gli occupancy and the co-option of tissue-specific inputs to produce new aspects of the patched expression pattern over time.

results.result: The Hedgehog signaling pathway is an ancient, conserved developmental signaling system among bilaterians that is pleiotropic in function and linked to human disease.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C7-C12 collectively establish well-documented background knowledge about the Hedgehog pathway. These claims are supported by citations to prior research and represent established facts in the field, providing appropriate context for the study.

results.result: A small number of Hedgehog pathway genes, including patched/Ptch1, respond to Hh signaling in a universal, constitutive manner, but the molecular basis for this constitutive response is not understood and no universal master response element has been found.
results.evaluation: Claims C13, C14, C16, and C17 establish the knowledge gap that motivates this study. These claims are supported by citations to prior research and accurately describe the state of the field, justifying the research question.

results.result: Patched functions as the Hedgehog receptor that inhibits Smoothened and is itself transcriptionally activated by Gli in all Hh-regulated tissues, forming a conserved negative feedback circuit essential for normal development.
results.evaluation: Claims C18-C22 describe the established mechanism of Hedgehog pathway regulation through Patched. These claims are well-supported by citations to prior research and represent fundamental knowledge about the pathway that provides necessary background.

results.result: The promoter-proximal enhancer ptcprox contains three optimal Gli binding sites required for wing expression but fails to respond to Hh/Gli in the embryonic ectoderm, indicating that the control region for embryonic stripe expression is located elsewhere in the locus.
results.evaluation: Claims C23-C29 present key experimental findings supported by data in Figures 1B-G. The tissue-specific activity of ptcprox is demonstrated through reporter assays, and the conclusion that embryonic control regions lie elsewhere is a logical inference from the data. This establishes a critical motivation for the locus-wide analysis.

results.result: The patched locus contains abundant, diverse enhancers with stage- and tissue-specific expression patterns distributed across the locus, with no single enhancer recapitulating the complete ptc expression pattern, and the constitutive Hh response is controlled by an unexpectedly complex multi-modular system of enhancers.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C30, C33-C37, C39-C42 present the central finding of the study supported by extensive experimental data in Figure 2 and throughout the manuscript. The systematic testing of enhancer fragments across the locus, combined with chromatin accessibility data and prior DamID data, provides strong evidence for the multi-modular architecture. This is a major discovery that challenges the simple model of constitutive gene regulation.

results.result: Multiple distinct embryonic stripe enhancers (1EH, VT, LK) drive expression in different subsets of ptc-positive cells in the embryonic ectoderm, with each enhancer showing specific spatial patterns relative to Hh-producing cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C46 describe specific embryonic enhancers and their expression patterns, supported by data in Figure 3 and supplementary figures. The spatial specificity of each enhancer is clearly demonstrated through reporter assays and imaging, and the Hh-responsiveness of LK is confirmed by overexpression experiments.

results.result: Low- to moderate-affinity Gli motifs are required for strong activation in the embryonic ectoderm, and optimizing Gli motifs to consensus sequences decreases enhancer activity in embryos but increases activity in wing discs, demonstrating that nonconsensus Gli motifs influence both strength and tissue specificity of Hedgehog responses.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C56 present a sophisticated analysis of Gli binding site affinity and its tissue-specific effects, supported by extensive mutagenesis experiments, EMSA data (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), and in vivo reporter assays (Figure 3). The counterintuitive finding that optimal Gli sites reduce embryonic activity is well-documented and consistent with prior work by the authors. The tissue-dependent effects of Gli site optimization are clearly demonstrated.

results.result: The ptc response to Hh/Gli in the wing is distributed across many enhancers that all depend on Gli motifs, but the number and quality of Gli motifs bears no obvious relationship to enhancer strength, indicating that Gli motif quality is not a good predictor of which enhancers will be most active in a given tissue.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C63 present findings on wing enhancers supported by data in Figure 4. The systematic comparison of multiple enhancers with different Gli binding site compositions, tested both in vivo and in cell culture, provides strong evidence that Gli site quality alone does not predict enhancer activity. The observation that ptcprox is weaker than other enhancers despite having optimal Gli sites is particularly compelling.

results.result: The promoter-proximal cluster of optimal Gli sites requires additional flanking sequences for strong activity in vivo, with 5' sequences containing few and weak Gli motifs providing significant boosts to expression, and transcriptional synergy observed among sub-fragments such that the activity of large fragments exceeds the sum of individual sub-fragments.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C73 describe nested deletion analysis of the promoter-proximal region supported by data in Figure 4F-K. The systematic testing of fragments of increasing size, combined with mutagenesis of the three optimal Gli sites, demonstrates both the requirement for flanking sequences and the synergistic interactions among enhancer elements. Statistical analysis (p<0.0015) supports the significance of the three optimal Gli sites.

results.result: The ptc promoter and 5' sequences show tissue-specific Polycomb/Trithorax regulation, with PcG binding and H3K27me3 marks in larvae but not embryos, and enhancers drive qualitatively different expression patterns when paired with the native ptc promoter versus a heterologous promoter, indicating that interactions among enhancers, promoter-proximal sequences, and the core promoter are integrated in a tissue-specific manner.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C90 present findings on promoter-enhancer interactions supported by ChIP-seq data (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1), sequence analysis (Figure 5B), and systematic promoter-swapping experiments (Figure 5C-D). The tissue-specific differences in PcG/TrxG regulation are well-documented through comparison of larval and embryonic ChIP-seq data. The functional consequences of promoter choice are clearly demonstrated through reporter assays.

results.result: Mouse Ptch1 and fly patched share a similar multi-enhancer regulatory structure, with multiple Gli-bound enhancers driving overlapping subsets of the Ptch1 expression pattern, no single enhancer recapitulating the complete pattern, dynamic Gli binding across developmental contexts, and both loci flanked by CTCF boundaries with enhancers acting through PcG-bound, H3K27me3-marked promoters.
results.evaluation: Claims C31, C92-C105 present comparative findings between mouse and fly supported by Gli ChIP-seq data (Figure 6B), transgenic mouse reporter assays (Figure 6A), H3K27me3 ChIP-seq (Figure 6C), and Hi-C/CTCF data (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). The parallel architecture between species is well-documented through multiple lines of evidence. This demonstrates the evolutionary conservation of the regulatory strategy.

results.result: The cis-regulatory architecture of patched/Ptch1 represents one of the oldest cis-regulatory features in animal genomes, allowing independent modulation of Hedgehog signaling levels in a stage- and tissue-specific manner without disturbing pathway activity in other contexts, enabling the gene to function as an adaptable tissue-specific modifier of pathway activity and substrate for morphological evolution.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C6, C32, C107-C111, C126, C128, C133 present the major conclusions of the study. These claims are well-supported by the extensive experimental data demonstrating the multi-modular architecture in both fly and mouse, the tissue-specific enhancer activities, the promoter-enhancer interactions, and the evolutionary conservation of the regulatory strategy. The conclusion that this architecture allows independent tuning in different tissues is a logical inference from the demonstrated tissue-specificity of individual enhancers.

results.result: The quality/affinity of Gli binding motifs is extremely important for proper patterning, with optimal activation achieved via suboptimal Gli binding sites in the embryo, possibly reflecting the dual activator/repressor function of Ci/Gli and the relatively high concentration of GliR in embryonic cells creating selective pressures favoring lower Gli occupancy.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C117 present mechanistic interpretations of the Gli binding site optimization data. While C112 is well-supported by experimental data, claims C115-C117 are speculative explanations for the observed phenomena. The proposed mechanism involving GliA:GliR ratios is plausible and supported by citations to prior work, but direct evidence for this mechanism is not provided in the current study. The speculation is reasonable but requires further experimental validation.

results.result: The large-scale cis-regulatory strategy is conserved between fly and vertebrate Ptch1, but the specific cis-regulatory sequences are not conserved across large evolutionary distances; instead, patched and its orthologs share an ancient regulatory structure composed of relatively young enhancers that evolved through tuning of Gli occupancy and co-option of tissue-specific inputs.
results.evaluation: Claims C118-C122 present an evolutionary model supported by the comparative data from mouse and fly. The lack of sequence conservation between species (C119) is documented through sequence analysis, while the conservation of regulatory structure (C118, C120) is demonstrated through the parallel multi-enhancer architecture. The proposed evolutionary mechanism (C121) is a reasonable inference from the data, though it remains somewhat speculative. The conclusion about conflicting requirements for different tissues (C122) is supported by the Gli site optimization experiments.

results.result: The cis-regulatory architecture of patched is a remarkably ancient example of gene regulatory strategy in animals, more conserved than comparable circuits like Notch-Hes/Hey regulation or Hox gene regulation, and this architecture has advantages of transcriptional precision and robustness while explaining reported cases of morphological divergence at the Ptch1 locus in bovine limbs and cichlid craniofacial structures.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C125, C127, C129-C132 place the findings in evolutionary context. The comparisons to other ancient regulatory circuits (C124, C125) are supported by citations to prior research. The connection to morphological evolution (C129-C131) is supported by citations to studies showing tissue-specific changes at Ptch1 that did not affect other developmental contexts, which is consistent with the multi-modular architecture discovered here. The advantages of the architecture (C127) are reasonable inferences supported by citations to shadow enhancer literature.

results.result: Hh signaling participates in the development and maintenance of multiple tissues including embryonic tissues, larval imaginal discs, and adult tissues such as the gut and stem cell/niche systems in testes and ovaries.
results.evaluation: Claim C38 is supported by citations to prior research and provides context for the tissue-specific enhancer analysis. This is established knowledge that justifies examining ptc regulation across multiple developmental contexts.

results.result: GAF has recently been implicated in large-scale changes in gene regulation during the embryo-larva transition.
results.evaluation: Claim C91 is supported by a citation to prior research and provides context for the observed tissue-specific differences in GAF occupancy at the ptc promoter.
